thread:
alex: Heads-up: customer 'NovaSearch' hit a rerank issue in a bulk payload. They POST multiple queries in one request and the response returns a single flat scores array that ends up misaligned with per-query candidate lists. Repro below — @maya can you take a look? cc @jorge :exclamation:

maya: Can you paste the exact payload + response you sent and any server logs you have?

alex: Sure — payload we sent (sanitized ids):
```json
{
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "query": "best laptops", "candidates": ["c1", "c2", "c3"]},
    {"id": "q2", "query": "budget phones", "candidates": ["c4", "c5"]}
  ],
  "options": {"mode": "rerank_batch"}
}
```

And the service returned (200 OK):
```json
{
  "scores": [0.8, 0.3, 0.9, 0.4, 0.2],
  "meta": {"total_candidates": 5}
}
```

alex: Issue: our SDK expects per-query score lists (i.e. [[...],[...]]), but the service flattened them. For most cases flattening is fine if consumer reconstructs using candidate counts, but NovaSearch's pipeline assumes nested arrays so ranks get mis-assigned — sometimes off-by-one. Their prod logs show mismatched mapping errors and downstream 400s.

jorge: Do we have any headers like `x-rerank-candidate-offsets` or similar returned? Any warnings in the logs? Also which SDK version was the client on? We pushed a csv/boundary fix earlier but not sure this path was covered.

alex: They used python-sdk v1.3.2. No special headers in the response besides standard content-type. Curl we ran against prod: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/bulk -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @payload.json -D -
```
Response headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 123
X-Request-Id: r-9f3e2
```
No extra mapping header.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-452 (severity: P1) by alex.

maya: I repro'd this against staging with the same payload. Looks like our server path that optimizes for flat buffering concatenates all candidate embeddings/scores into one vector and returns a flat `scores` array for throughput. We used to include `candidate_offsets` in the response for deterministic mapping; that field appears missing in prod for this endpoint variant. Without offsets the client must infer boundaries from the input candidate counts — that's brittle and the customer uses a different reconstruction.

jorge: Quick mitigation: client can send an explicit `candidate_offsets` array in the request so we echo it back and mapping is unambiguous. Example: add `"candidate_offsets": [0, 3]` (offsets are cumulative start indices). Try that and see if NovaSearch accepts it.

alex: They're in prod — patching customer SDK across many services will take time. This is causing billing headaches since retries + bad downstream handling trigger extra calls. Need short-term server-side shim or response compatibility for older clients.

maya: I'll open a hotfix PR to change the response to include `per_query_scores` (nested) for backward compatibility and also restore `candidate_offsets` when we detect a multi-query flattening path. @jorge can you own the runtime change? ETA EOD? :thumbsup:

jorge: On it. Plan: detect if `scores` is flat and `queries` present, then construct `per_query_scores` using client-provided candidate lengths or inferred offsets. Emit a server warning in logs and an `X-Rerank-Version: compat-1` header so we can track who relies on the old shape. I'll post the PR link once ready.

alex: Thanks. I've attached full prod request/response dumps to the incident and added repro unit tests that assert mapping works for different candidate length combos (including empty candidate lists). Will follow up when customer confirms.

sophie: Noted — tagging Billing to whitelist spike traffic while we patch.

maya: Follow-ups: (1) Add an integration test for nested vs flattened responses, (2) Update SDK to prefer `per_query_scores` when present and fall back to offsets, (3) Document `candidate_offsets` in the API spec.

alex: Perfect. Closing loop once PR lands and customer validates. :eyes:
